title: Getting a trumpet and starting to play with Bob Conry
summary: Bull talks his mother into a trumpet, Bob Conry gets a clarinet, and they fumble through Wolverine Blues; the interviewer checks that George is George Lewis.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: And we weren't interested in that at all. I wasn't. So we used to go to the jazz club every Saturday night from then on and listen and so on and so. And, as I say, I'd, I'd, I'd played the bugle. Mm-hmm. And I, I'd, just around about, just before that stage, I'd, I'd managed to bully my mother into buying me a trumpet. Mm-hmm. Which I was going to learn to play and I had a few lessons on, on, on the trumpet just to sort of, you know, I started off having lessons. I didn't know I was going to stop having lessons. I started off having lessons and they always teach the fingerings and all this stuff first. Anyway, and then we started getting some jazz. And one of the other fellas who was in the, in the crowd with us, uh, Bob Conry, he, he, he'd been listening for a while too and he was, uh, he was mad on George. And, uh, he'd bought himself a clarinet and he wanted to learn to play the clarinet and he just happened to mention one night, he said, oh, you know, I've got a clarinet. And I said, well, I've got a trumpet. And at that stage of the game, we'd never even sort of entertained the idea of actually playing this music, you know. I said, oh, well, I've got a trumpet. And he said, oh, I've got a clarinet. And then Jeff Holden didn't play anything so he got a washboard, obviously. Mm-hmm. And then we used to, uh, just get together and, and when we'd play records, we'd occasionally have a bit of a fiddle around and, uh, and we sort of, uh, bought, I can remember we went out and bought a book full of, you know, these, uh, books of Dixieland tunes. Mm-hmm. They have them over there, sort of, Dixie, stock Dixieland arrangements, you know, and they had things like, I remember one of them was Wolverine Blues. And we learnt Wolverine Blues, we thought, which was, uh, the, the, the first bit of the chorus, which goes, da, da, da, you know, that bit. We could play those three notes, uh, but after that, it got difficult, we had to stop, go back and start again. But anyway, we got sort of, uh, we got started off in, in that way. Now, this was, this is all, um, Can I stop you?

Yeah. You said the clarinet player like George, who is George? I'm assuming George Lewis. Uh, well, yeah, that's correct. Yeah. Yeah. Well, I'm sorry, I used that term in a too familiar way. Yeah. Well, naturally you would, but I, you know, I just want to make it clear.
Yeah. Well, getting back to what I was about to say, I'm, I'm sort of…
